The canonical quotient-to-image isomorphism is distinct from the original map into U; a square materially clarifies the exact image target and its inclusion into U, and the representative formula makes commutativity immediate.

correction: Added a tikzcd square V -> U, V/ker T -> im T with q downward, the induced isomorphism along the bottom, and image inclusion upward. Added explanatory prose specifying iota composed with T-tilde composed with q equals T.

diagram_math_checks.result: T: V -> U is the given linear map. q: V -> V/ker T is v -> v+ker T; the quotient is defined because ker T is a linear subspace by L2. The lower map T-tilde: V/ker T -> im T is exactly the Statement and proof step 1.1. The upward hooked arrow iota: im T -> U is the inclusion of the image subspace, justified by L2.

diagram_math_checks.check: Well-defined lower map and isomorphism label
diagram_math_checks.result: For v-v' in ker T, T(v)=T(v'), so T-tilde is independent of the representative by L1/the quotient universal property. Proof step 1.1 proves its linearity and surjectivity, and step 2.1 proves injectivity; hence the displayed isomorphism marker is valid, including zero-map and zero-space cases.

For y in im T, define the inverse value as v+ker T for any v satisfying T(v)=y. Such v exists by the image definition. Any two such representatives differ by ker T, so the coset is unique. Thus the compositions on cosets and on image elements are identities. This verifies the isomorphism marker without incorrectly identifying im T with U or asserting T itself is invertible.

For each v in V, (iota composed with T-tilde composed with q)(v)=iota(T(v))=T(v) in U by the exact Statement formula and proof step 1.1. The alternative route is the displayed top arrow T. There are exactly four arrows: V -> U, V -> V/ker T, V/ker T -> im T, and im T -> U. No surjectivity of the inclusion is asserted.
